pr_body:
Fix #913 

I updated all docs to promote good practice.

This should be handled as minor change. The charset of JSON is `utf8`. The default charset of `text` isn't given but we can protect users against crazy misinterpretations. `utf8` [is widely adopted](https://w3techs.com/technologies/overview/character_encoding/all) and defacto standard and most supported charset.

#### Checklist

- [X] run `npm run test` and `npm run benchmark`
- [ ] tests and/or benchmarks are included
- [X] documentation is changed or added
- [X] commit message and code follows [Code of conduct](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/master/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
pr_comments: I think a case could be made that this is a major change. Except, `application/json` is supposed to be UTF-8 by specification. So it could be a bug fix.

Due to the fact, that a receiver could have a different default charset as `utf8` for text we have a major change but:

I want to handle it as minor because it's very unlikely that fastify is used to transfer plain text outside of the browser and in the browser utf8 is defacto standard.
@mcollina did you noticed https://github.com/shieldfy/API-Security-Checklist/issues/25 ? Why don't cover it for free when we don't break things?
@mcollina yes, the spec requires JSON to be UTF-8. But that doesn't mean clients always transfer it as UTF-8 when the character set isn't explicitly set. There isn't any harm in being explicit here.

What do other Node.js framework do in this case? 

There was some discussion inhttps://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/380.

* Hapi: Default to utf-8 but configurable [here](https://github.com/hapijs/hapi/blob/08734ba720c788a86d9522253a7b601476052937/lib/response.js#L46)
* Koa: Default to utf-8 [here](https://github.com/koajs/koa/blob/d394724200d0e36e6af6db2edb524820212da915/test/response/type.js#L22)
* Echo (Golang): Default to utf-8 [here](https://github.com/labstack/echo/blob/f867058e3ba4fa4504e3ca976b31012db3ce1555/echo.go#L148)

> There was some discussion in https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/380.

Correct, but read the later comments (in the linked issue of the Akka Project) and read the security vulnerability it's an annoying topic and can be fixed by forcing the default charset.

@mcollina or here from changelog of express 4.16.0

> Set charset as "UTF-8" for .js and .json
Many frameowork and browser use `application/json; charset=utf-8` instead `application/json;charset=utf-8` opinions?
They are technically equivalent but the extra space is more legible.
This pull request has been automatically locked since there has not been any recent activity after it was closed. Please open a new issue for related bugs.

issue_context.title: Use UTF8 as default charset for Text and JSON
issue_context.body:
Hi, when I return a string like `ÄÜÖ` the browser is interpreted as
```
Ã„ÃœÃ–
```
fastify will respond with
```
content-type: text/html;
content-type: application/json;
```
it's obvious that I use the wrong charset but UTF8 is defacto standard and should be used as default.
```
content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
```

> A Unicode encoding such as UTF-8 is a good choice for a number of [reasons](https://www.w3.org/International/questions/qa-choosing-encodings).

References:
* https://www.w3.org/International/questions/qa-choosing-encodings
* https://www.w3.org/International/articles/http-charset/index#charset
comments:
`application/json` is `utf-8` by default, but Fastify could use `text/plain; charset=utf-8` here:
https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/2907be7c5352926eda073c5a4be7701f7de39006/lib/reply.js#L66

I recommend to enforce utf8 for json due to security reason

https://github.com/shieldfy/API-Security-Checklist/issues/25
I will prepare a PR or already done? @nwoltman 😄
